note: Shipped remediation playbooks. Add your own to data/playbooks_local.json (never overwritten by an update); see docs/PLAYBOOKS.md for the format.

playbooks.impact: After a takeover the node ({node}) stays down until someone gives it back, leaving the pair without redundancy.
steps: 1. Check: storage failover show -fields auto-giveback,possible
2. Enable: storage failover modify -node * -auto-giveback true
3. Confirm: storage failover show -fields auto-giveback
options: Option A: Enable on all nodes (recommended).

playbooks.cause: Fewer than two external NTP servers are configured.
playbooks.impact: Cluster time can drift, which breaks Kerberos/AD authentication, certificates, log correlation and SnapMirror schedules.
steps: 1. Check: cluster time-service ntp server show ; cluster time-service ntp status show
2. Add at least a second, independent source: cluster time-service ntp server create -server <ntp-server-2>
3. Use three or more servers where possible so a faulty source can be outvoted; prefer internal stratum 2-3 servers.
4. Check: cluster time-service ntp status show ; date
options: Option A: Three NTP servers, two internal and one external (recommended).

playbooks.match: one or more ntp servers are not responding
playbooks.cause: An NTP server configured on the cluster does not answer.
playbooks.impact: Cluster time can drift, which breaks Kerberos/AD authentication, certificates, log correlation and SnapMirror schedules.
steps: 1. Check: cluster time-service ntp server show ; cluster time-service ntp status show

2. Test reachability from the cluster network (UDP 123): network ping -lif <mgmt-lif> -vserver {cluster} -destination <ntp-server>; remove a dead server: cluster time-service ntp server delete -server <dead-ntp>
3. Use three or more servers where possible so a faulty source can be outvoted; prefer internal stratum 2-3 servers.
4. Check: cluster time-service ntp status show ; date
options: Option A: Three NTP servers, two internal and one external (recommended).

playbooks.match: vserver has a single dns server configured
playbooks.impact: If it is unavailable, name resolution, AD authentication and SMB/NFS access fail.
steps: 1. Check: vserver services name-service dns show -vserver {svm}
2. Add the second server (keep the existing one first): vserver services name-service dns modify -vserver {svm} -domains <domain> -name-servers <dns1>,<dns2>
3. Check: vserver services name-service dns check -vserver {svm}
options: Option A: Two or more DNS servers in different locations (recommended).

playbooks.match: certificate validation is set to false for fabricpool
playbooks.cause: The FabricPool object store accepts any certificate.
playbooks.impact: Tiered data could be sent to an impostor endpoint (man-in-the-middle).
steps: 1. Check: storage aggregate object-store config show -fields server,ssl-enabled,is-certificate-validation-enabled
2. Install the CA that signed the object store certificate: security certificate install -type server-ca -vserver {cluster}
3. Turn validation on: storage aggregate object-store config modify -object-store-name <object-store> -is-certificate-validation-enabled true
4. Check the tiering still works: storage aggregate object-store show-space ; storage aggregate show -fields tiering-policy
options: Option A: Install the CA and enable validation (recommended).

playbooks.cause: Replication traffic between the clusters is not encrypted.
playbooks.impact: SnapMirror data and metadata cross the network in clear text.
steps: 1. Check: cluster peer show -fields encryption-protocol-proposed,encryption-protocol,auth-status-admin

2. Enable on this cluster: cluster peer modify -cluster <peer-cluster> -auth-status-admin use-authentication -encryption-protocol-proposed tls-psk  (do the same on the peer; the passphrase is generated and exchanged for you in 9.6 and later).
3. Check: cluster peer show -fields encryption-protocol ; snapmirror show -fields status
options: Option A: TLS-PSK on every peer relationship (recommended).
playbooks.thirdParty: Do the change on both clusters in the same window; a mismatch stops transfers until both agree.

ticket.window: Both clusters in the same window; transfers pause until both agree

playbooks.match: system has not converted to either netapp license fi?le \(nlf\)
playbooks.cause: The cluster still has 28-character license keys instead of NetApp license files.
playbooks.impact: Old keys are no longer issued; capacity and feature changes need NLF, and entitlement checks can fail after an upgrade.
steps: 1. List what is installed: system license show -fields package,type,expiration
2. Sign in to the NetApp Support Site (My Support, Software Licenses), enter the cluster serial numbers (system node show -fields serialnumber for {cluster}) and download the NLF for each.
3. Install: system license add -license-code <contents of the NLF>  (one per serial number).
4. Check: system license show-status
options: Option A: Install NLF for every node serial (recommended).

playbooks.cause: SSH/Telnet remote login to the controllers of {model} is enabled.
playbooks.impact: Remote login is meant for NetApp Support at their request. Left on, it gives anyone who can reach the controller management network a shell prompt to attack.
steps: 1. Confirm with the storage team that NetApp Support is not working on the array now.
2. In SANtricity System Manager open Hardware, then the Controllers & Components tab, and select controller A.
3. Select Configure remote login (SSH) (named Change remote login in SANtricity 11.73 and earlier), clear the Enable remote login checkbox and confirm. Active connections end.
4. Repeat for controller B: the setting is per controller.
5. If NetApp Support needs it later, turn it on for the session only. On SANtricity 11.74 and later you can also require an SSH key or password for remote login.
options: Option A: Disable on both controllers (recommended).
Option B: Keep it on only while a support case needs it, and record who turned it off again.

ticket.window: Any; open shell sessions to the controller end
ticket.rollback: Tick Enable remote login again in Configure remote login (SSH) on each controller.
